segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I wanted to confirm the scope we talked about: 42 user seats for the calibration management platform, plus the initial import of your gauge list from the two plants.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That's right. It's 42 seats to start, and the gauge list is about 3,800 records. We may add the Ohio service team later, but not for this contract.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. For the first year, that puts the subscription at $28,560, and the one-time implementation is $6,400. That includes the import, admin training, and two technician training sessions.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. And the invoice timing, can that be net 30 after signature? Our finance team is closing July pretty tight.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, net 30 after signature is fine. If you sign by August 9, the invoice would go out the same week, and payment would be due 30 days from invoice date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. On go-live, we're trying to be ready by September 23 because our internal audit starts October 7.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: That timeline is reasonable. We'd schedule kickoff the week of August 12, target the data import review by September 6, and then training the week of September 16.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. One question on the contract term: it's a 12-month term, and then renewal at the same seat count unless we change it, correct?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. Twelve months from the start date, with renewal pricing based on the seats you have at that time. Any added seats during the year are prorated to the renewal date.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send me the order form with 42 seats and the September 23 go-live target, and I'll route it to procurement.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send it over this afternoon with the net 30 language and the implementation schedule attached.
